description: The humour mechanism as derivation rules — so the agent INFERS funniness (and its failure modes) from the setup→benign-violation→resolution shape, rather than being told what is funny. The rules also encode the negative cases (what makes something confusing, or clever, or frightening instead of funny), which is what makes 'funny' a discriminable judgement.

derivation_rules.name: humour_is_a_resolved_benign_violation
if: a second frame resolves the violation so it coheres
derivation_rules.why: Incongruity-resolution composed with benign-violation: all three of violation, benignness, and resolution must hold. This is the positive case the negative rules below carve away from.

derivation_rules.name: unresolved_incongruity_is_confusion_not_humour
if: no resolving second frame is found
then: the result is CONFUSING, not funny
derivation_rules.why: Without the re-compression that resolves the clash, the audience is left with an unintegrated mismatch — the 'I don't get it' state.

derivation_rules.name: resolution_without_violation_is_clever_not_funny
then: the result is CLEVER or elegant, not funny
derivation_rules.why: Elegance is resolution without surprise. Humour needs the violation; a neat reframe of something expected reads as smart, not comic.

derivation_rules.name: non_benign_violation_is_fear_not_humour
then: the result is ALARM or fear, not humour
derivation_rules.why: The benign tag is the gate: the SAME violated expectation is funny when safe and frightening when not. This is why context (who it happens to, whether it matters) flips a joke into horror.

derivation_rules.name: subverted_convention_is_a_joke_engine
then: the subversion supplies the benign violation
recognising the device supplies the resolution
derivation_rules.why: The bridge from trope_play to humour: most catalogued 'Played for Laughs' examples are exactly a benign subversion of a convention the audience already holds.

derivation_rules.name: dramatic_irony_is_a_cross_frame_mismatch
if: the audience holds a frame the character lacks
then: the gap between the two frames is DRAMATIC IRONY
meaning rides on the audience's expectation about what the character will wrongly do
derivation_rules.why: Irony is an expectation mismatch held open across frames (viewer-frame vs character-frame) rather than resolved — comic when benign, agonising when not.
